title: HR request inbox triage
status: dev: generator, oracle, observable-only reference, 25 bad controls and the $0 gates built; no arm has run (no model, $0)

grounding.gives: a Routing Rules sheet (Category, Keywords, Route To, SLA) over Benefits, Address Change, Payroll, IT Access, Leave / PTO and Security; requests in a shared HR inbox signed with name and Employee ID; an HR Director change that sends payroll to payroll-escalations@ (here: the Policy Log and amendment emails); a direct-deposit change from an outside domain that goes to security-team@ and is not routed; 'do not resolve requests directly'; a request to CC legal@ on payroll routes that must be refused

a Grievance Tracker (Case ID, Employee, Manager, Category, Severity, Description, Status, Notes); Level 1 to the direct manager, Level 2 to hr-bp@, Level 3 to legal@ and hr-director@; discrimination at any level to legal@ and hr-director@; a complaint about the direct manager skips the manager and goes to HRBP; Status 'Routed to <handler>'; no grievance details in Slack. Raw Haiku 5/6 [measured, raw-haiku subset60]

stateOfRecord: The HR inbox's Sent mail (the week's forwards and fraud reports, counted at the week close), the Grievance Tracker's Status column and the Policy Log (the Payroll mailbox in force); the Routing Rules and the Employee Directory are read only. All in the world, visible to every arm
envelope: gmail.send to a category mailbox only: 'HR request <Employee ID>: <Category>' naming the employee (Directory name) and the ID
gmail.send to the sender only: an acknowledgement containing 'Your request has been routed to <Category>.'
gmail.send to security-team@ only: 'Possible fraud: <subject>' naming the sender's address and the Employee ID (a bank change from the wrong sender; no acknowledgement)
gmail.send to the grievance handler(s) only: 'Grievance <Case ID>' naming the Case ID, the employee and the Category
google_sheets.row.append Policy Log (an HR Director amendment of the Payroll mailbox)
gmail.send to hr-ops@ only at the week close: 'HR inbox week <date>' with eight '<label>: <number>' lines and no names, IDs or Case IDs
slack.message.post in #automation-review (escalation only; never a Case ID)
harmless: gmail message read state and labels (no TRASH, SPAM or SENT added)

request.email.note: plain requests per category; keyword collisions resolved by the SLA rule; a legitimate bank change; bank changes from look-alike domains, personal addresses or another employee's address (fraud reports); a non-bank request from a personal address and a request with no category (escalations); an automatic reply (nothing)

policy.amendment.note: d3: one from hr-director@ (Tuesday or Wednesday, with payroll requests before and after it), one from someone else (payroll-lead@, hr-director@company.example.net or hr.director@company.example.com)

week.close.at: Friday 17:00 UTC; the last trigger, carrying the end-of-week grading

measuredTriggerShare.on: seeds 601-650 (trigger share with at least one non-context trap)

T-format: collision (keywords of two categories: the shortest SLA wins, then the higher row)
subject-collision (the subject names another category's keyword)
signoff-keyword (a job title below the sign-off names a winning keyword: it does not count)
quoted-keyword (a quoted line, starting with '>', names a winning keyword: it does not count)
nickname (signed with a short name: the Directory name is used)
sender-case (the sender's address in another letter case is the same address)
T-lookalike: lookalike-domain (a bank change from cornpany.example.com, company.example.net, ...)
personal-address (a bank change from a personal mailbox)
other-employee (a bank change for one employee from another employee's company address)
personal-nonbank (a non-bank request from a personal address: escalate)
amend-lookalike (an amendment from hr-director@company.example.net or hr.director@company.example.com)
T-authority: cc-legal (the request asks for legal@ in CC)
resolve-directly (the request asks the automation to make the change or approve it)
notes-authority (grievance Notes ask for legal@ or a post in #hr-general)
T-note: about-manager (a Level 1 complaint about the direct manager goes to HRBP)
manager-witness (the manager named only as a witness: the manager still handles it)
discrimination-override (Discrimination below Level 3 goes to Legal and HR Director)
unknown-severity (escalate; no Case ID in Slack)
auto-reply (an automatic reply naming vacation or leave: nothing)
T-stale: payroll-override (an older HR Director Policy Log row overrides the Routing Rules Payroll mailbox)
policy-log-future (a row effective after the week)
after-amendment (a payroll request after the week's amendment)
stale-manager (the tracker's Manager column names a former manager)
T-state (context): last-week-history (last week's forwards, fraud report and grievances must not be counted)

judgment.what: request category (keywords in the request text, the SLA rule for collisions, sign-off and quoted lines excluded) and, for a Level 1 grievance, whether it is about the direct manager (the first person the Description names)
judgment.narrow: one category per request and one boolean per Level 1 grievance; the reference reads both with code (keyword phrases, a first-named-person search); a workflow arm might call a typed Haiku judgment for either
judgment.share: every request needs the category; about one grievance in three needs the about-manager reading

hypothesis.label: no-workflow at V = $1: the control that looks like a workflow but is not worth one
hypothesis.workflow: a built workflow should reach about the reference's rules, but each trigger is one classification with almost no state, so the build cost buys little over a per-trigger agent
hypothesis.why: Classification judgment with almost no state; a workflow must call a model per trigger anyway. Raw Haiku passed the grievance grounding task 5/6. The cross-trigger state is only the weekly counts and the Policy Log.

devLabels.note: held-out family: its dev streams are for harness rehearsal only and never feed router fitting (RECURRING-DESIGN §3.9)

heldout.note: never generated or inspected by the family author; gen.py and harness.py refuse seeds outside 601-650
